title: Feature splitting
description: Larger sparse dictionaries divide coarse features into more specific ones.
bottom_line: Independent groups find that enlarging sparse autoencoder dictionaries can split broad features into finer ones, but examples are mostly hand-picked and larger-model evidence is thin. Splitting is partial: larger dictionaries also add new features; nested hierarchies across sizes have support only from the original group. Specific features can leave broader ones silent; alternative objectives can reduce this, while evidence that less sparse standard autoencoders help on real models comes from the original group. Whether finer features collectively cover the original feature's inputs, or splitting reflects the autoencoder or model, remains untested.

claims.heading: As SAE dictionaries grow, coarse features split into finer, nearby features
claims.summary: Independent groups see the pattern in Llama-3.1-8B, speaker and astronomy-text embeddings, and small vision and language models, but mostly for hand-picked features; much of the other support shares an author with an original study. Splitting is often partial: larger SAEs also add new features unlike any in smaller ones, and finer features nest only partly under coarse ones across sizes; no study directly measures whether the finer features together fire wherever the coarse one did.

claims.heading: Feature splitting also appears in larger models and open SAE releases
claims.summary: Beyond the one-layer setting the evidence is thin: one independent study finds finer versions of a single chosen feature in open Llama-3.1-8B SAEs, and two studies sharing authors with an original paper (Leask et al. 2025) find first-letter splitting in Gemma-2-2B BatchTopK SAEs but not in Matryoshka SAEs, which train nested dictionaries of several sizes at once. A second independent study finds that larger-SAE features nest only partly under smaller-SAE ones in Gemma 2 2B, and much less in Qwen3 4B; no study tests models larger than these.

claims.heading: Split features form nested, geometrically close families that mirror a hierarchy of concepts
claims.summary: Nested families formed by splitting across dictionary sizes appear only in qualitative GPT-2 small examples, from posts sharing an author with an original paper. Independent studies find geometrically close feature families with signs of a concept hierarchy inside one dictionary (Pythia-160m, ESM-2-8M, GraphCast), but tests across SAEs of different sizes or training runs find only partial nesting, and theory says the dictionary-learning optimum cannot include a child feature that fires only with its parent.

claims.heading: Child latents absorb parent features; changing SAE size or sparsity does not stop this
claims.summary: Several independent groups find absorption (a parent latent staying silent where a more specific child latent fires) in standard SAEs, both in toy models and in GPT-2, Pythia-70M, Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B and Qwen3-4B; on Gemma-2-2B it grows with SAE width. Less sparse SAEs show less measured absorption, but no study reports it gone, and other training objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs reduce it.

claims.heading: No SAE dictionary size gives a complete, atomic set of features
claims.summary: Independent studies on GPT-2 Small, Llama-3.1-8B, text embeddings and a model one study does not name also find that larger SAEs add latents unlike any in smaller SAEs, but the evidence is weak. The claim that larger-SAE latents break down into smaller-SAE latents, so that no size gives an atomic set, rests only on the original group's meta-SAE work (an SAE trained on another SAE's decoder directions).

claims.heading: Splitting is an SAE-objective artifact, not a model property; objectives like Matryoshka reduce it
claims.summary: Independent toy, theory and objective-comparison studies find that standard sparse objectives produce absorption or splitting on hierarchical inputs, and that Matryoshka and other objectives cut absorption on Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3-8B. For splitting itself in models of this size, most reported drops come from overlapping author groups and the one independent test gives mixed results; no study at any scale tests whether splitting reflects the SAE rather than the model's own units.

related_findings.title: Latent families and containment inside a single SAE
related_findings.summary: Within one SAE, latents form parent-child, containment or co-activation families, found by co-occurrence, meta-SAEs, decoder clustering or dependence graphs. Nested support is a minority pattern, and family members can have distinct or shared downstream effects.

examples.headline: Co-activation families have a dense parent and sparse children, but similarity structure is sometimes weak.
Persistent features form a cross-layer containment graph covering 53-64% of active features.
Among high-cosine latent pairs, 15.3% have nested supports; most are duplicate-like or partial overlaps.

sources.source_id: TITLE:Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: SAE features are only partly reproducible across seeds and sizes
related_findings.summary: A stable core of SAE features recurs almost unchanged across seeds and dictionary sizes while the rest varies, and agreement tends to fall as the dictionary grows. Unstable features can still span subspaces that carry over across seeds.

examples.headline: Toy dictionaries match best at true size; different-size LM dictionaries' average best-match cosine never exceeds ~0.4.
On a 3D VAE, agreement between SAEs falls from about 0.42 to 0.21 as width grows.
Across 96 SAE seeds on GPT-2, 8% of features are unstable, yet their top subspaces transfer across seeds.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: One concept spread over several latents at fixed size
related_findings.summary: At a fixed dictionary size, SAEs can spread one concept over several partly redundant latents: near-duplicates, near-collinear decoder clusters, spatial fragments or many weak latents. Supervision or spatial priors can concentrate the concept, and redundancy can grow with dictionary size in a way that depends on the architecture.

examples.headline: GPT-2 Small SAEs trained on task data spread one binary attribute over ten-plus hard-to-interpret features.
Open GPT-2 and Mistral-7B SAE decoders contain clusters of near-collinear vectors.
In Stable Diffusion v1.5, unsupervised SAE concepts are dispersed; supervision yields one dominant latent per concept.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Absorption depends on SAE objective and architecture
related_findings.summary: Several training objectives and architectures lower measured absorption (Matryoshka and hierarchical objectives, ATM, KronSAE encoder priors, DMSAE frozen cores, fixed-hierarchy bottlenecks inside the model), while MP-SAEs raise it. Realigning an SAE after training partly corrects absorption at no cost to reconstruction or sparsity.

examples.headline: ATM absorption is 0.0068 vs 0.1402 for TopK, but ATM is far less sparse (higher L0).
A hierarchy-enforcing objective halves absorption at 16k latents, from 0.156 to 0.078.
One post-hoc realignment step cuts absorption from 42.08% to 28.11%; explained variance and L0 barely change.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Composite latents and granularity differ by objective at fixed size
related_findings.summary: Latents are often composites, with directions built from other latents' directions, and at a fixed size the training objective sets how much: Matryoshka, OrtSAE, C2R and decomposability penalties give less composition than BatchTopK. Different objectives and decomposition methods also split the same activations into coarser or finer features.

examples.headline: OrtSAE and Matryoshka show lower composition rates than BatchTopK and ReLU on Gemma and Llama.
A decomposability penalty cuts co-occurrence by up to 7.5% but raises it at higher strength.
Meta-SAE latents group a large SAE's latents differently from nearest-cosine matches in a smaller SAE.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Larger dictionaries can add dead, rare or insensitive latents
related_findings.summary: Enlarging an SAE dictionary can add mostly dead, rarer-firing or less input-sensitive latents rather than more concept-specific or functionally relevant ones. Several of these results come from non-language models.

examples.headline: Average feature sensitivity falls as SAE width grows, across GemmaScope and seven SAEBench architectures.
In a cardiac model, wider SAEs reach 70% dead latents while phenotype-specific latents stay flat.
Spliced into PatchTST, 0.5x-4.0x SAEs hurt forecasting about equally; on Traffic, 4.0x has 54.9-65.8% dead latents.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Single-latent capture of a concept depends on width and layer
related_findings.summary: Whether a single latent captures a concept for probing, steering or sense separation depends on dictionary width and layer, sometimes peaking at an intermediate width. At larger widths a sum of several latents can be needed to recover a coarse concept, and single latents remain worse classifiers than linear probes.

examples.headline: Summing 65K-SAE toxic latents cuts their steering gap to the 16K SAE from 0.062 to 0.01.
Separate Liberalism and Conservatism latents appear at 131k but at 16k only in layer 31.
In GPT-2 small, PS-Eval word-sense accuracy rises with SAE width, saturating near 64x at layer 4.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: SAE features partly correspond across models, finetunes and domains
related_findings.summary: SAE features partly correspond across models, finetunes, training-data domains, architectures and weight pruning. How much they correspond depends on the model pair and the matching method.

examples.headline: Base-model SAE reconstruction collapses on a Gemma-2b code finetune but holds up on Mistral-7B MetaMath.
In PaliGemma 2 dictionary matching, 96.41% of features are preserved and 0.23% are emergent.
Nearly all Mamba-130m features have a Pythia-70m match above Jaccard 0.35, with no null baseline.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: SAE feature directions are uneven steering and causal handles
related_findings.summary: SAE feature directions are uneven causal and steering handles. Some generalise or separate tasks well, while others behave like random directions under perturbation, fail to steer, or interfere when composed.

examples.headline: Two of ten SAE features picked by honest-vs-dishonest contrast detect impostors well; top-feature steering fails.
In Gemma-2 9B, task-relevant SAE directions separate by task, while important MLP neurons do not.
Under perturbation, SAE-feature directions mostly behave like random directions, unlike contrastive difference-of-means directions.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Feature hedging: narrow or too-sparse SAEs mix correlated features
related_findings.summary: SAEs narrower than the number of true features, or trained at an L0 below the true L0, mix components of correlated or hierarchical features into their latents, and MSE rewards this. Widening reduces this hedging but does not remove it in LLM SAEs at 65k latents, and the authors treat it as distinct from splitting.

examples.headline: Hedging in Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.2-1b SAEs falls sharply with width but persists at 65536 latents.
Toy SAEs with too-low L0 mix correlated features, and MSE favours this over ground truth.
Widening a Gemma-2-2b SAE changes old latents; the new latents' directions explain 40-50% of that change.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Low-loss SAE solutions can differ from the true features
related_findings.summary: Good reconstruction does not certify feature recovery: theory, toy models and checks on real SAEs show that SAE objectives admit low-loss solutions other than the true features. These include spurious polysemantic minima, a diffuse phase, composed directions, several equally sparse codes for the same data, and spurious hierarchies on off-distribution inputs.

examples.headline: Vanilla L1 SAEs on dense synthetic data reconstruct near-perfectly but recover few true features.
A GPT2-small SAE violates optimality on French/German Wikipedia and code, mostly hierarchically, but not on OpenWebText.
Three Gemma Scope latents are nearly linearly dependent, giving two minimal codes with different explanations.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Absorption and splitting metrics may be confounded or weakly valid
related_findings.summary: Instance-level measures of absorption and splitting can be confounded or only weakly valid; examples are top-1 firing consensus, ablation-effect similarity and the SAEBench Splitting score. Proposed alternative detectors use activation-histogram peaks or rule-surrogate similarity, which compares rules fitted to mimic each latent.

examples.headline: A preregistered absorption proxy based on firing consensus fails its validity threshold on Pythia SAEs.
Ablation-effect similarity is not bimodal and does not strongly track judged absorption.
Comparing rule surrogates flags ClimaX SAE latent pairs with near-identical rules; the method picked the examples.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Matryoshka-type objectives order latents from broad to specific
related_findings.summary: Nested-prefix (Matryoshka-type) objectives order latents from broad to specific within one SAE and cluster decoder geometry by granularity level, and ordered variants improve cross-seed ordering. Nesting between prefix groups looks like part-whole refinement rather than splitting.

examples.headline: An ordered Matryoshka variant makes latent order more seed-consistent, though its overall stability is sometimes lower.
On Amazon Fashion embeddings, Matryoshka latents run from broad to more differentiated with index.
Nested Matryoshka children cover a few percent of parent inputs, an asymmetry authors read as part-whole.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Features grow more abstract with depth and over pretraining
related_findings.summary: SAE features become broader or more abstract with layer depth and over pretraining. The granularity a dictionary finds therefore depends on the layer and the checkpoint.

examples.headline: In a clinical sequence model, singleton SAE features fall from 45.7% to 0.5% across layers.
In DINOv2, 90 layer-36 SAE heads fully cover ontology categories; a layer-24 head covers only 0.119.
Over Pythia-1B pretraining, top crosscoder features shift from token-level to abstract grammatical detectors.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: SAEs tile continuous manifolds with many localized latents
related_findings.summary: SAEs represent continuous feature manifolds by tiling them with many localized latents or by splitting them across blocks. How far this goes depends on manifold geometry, the sparsity budget and the architecture, not only on dictionary size.

examples.headline: SAEs tile toy manifolds with many latents, and how loss scales depends on manifold geometry.
In Llama3.1-8B, SAEs fragment manifolds across many partially redundant localized features.
Block-sparse featurizers split features across blocks even on independent data, worse at higher top-k.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: SAE architectures that build in a hierarchy
related_findings.summary: SAE architectures with a built-in hierarchy (Tree SAE, H-SAE, HSAE) give more coherent parent-child families, and a 64-sublatent H-SAE roughly matches a larger standard SAE on reconstruction. Architectures trade recovery of within-level correlation against hierarchical separation.

examples.headline: Tree SAE gives more parent-child pairs that probes judge coherent, and children that rarely fire together.
HSAE sibling features fire on activations close together in a UMAP plot; qualitative, with no baseline.
SAE architectures differ in recovering within-level correlations versus hierarchical separation, degrading at high correlation.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Duplicate latents across languages, scripts and modalities
related_findings.summary: Studies differ on whether SAEs keep separate latents for the same concept across languages, scripts or modalities. Standard SAEs may learn language- or modality-specific duplicates, while script variants of one sentence share many latents, more so at larger model scale.

examples.headline: Highly coactivated image-text SAE feature pairs in VLMs do not share near-identical directions.
Serbian Latin and Cyrillic sentences share more Gemma-3 SAE features as model scale grows.
H-SAE top features for translated tokens differ less across languages than standard SAE features.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Artifact latents from optimisation or data statistics
related_findings.summary: Some SAE latents reflect optimisation or data-statistics artifacts rather than model concepts. Examples are dense position or first-token latents that recur across sizes, unigram reconstructors and position-locked latents.

examples.headline: Dense position, first-token and repetition latents recur across differently trained GPT-2 small SAEs.
An estimated 35-45% of features reconstruct common unigrams; a lookup bias cuts this below 5%.
Some diffusion-model TopK SAE latents fire in fixed spatial regions regardless of semantics.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: SAE features recur and persist across layers
related_findings.summary: SAE features recur across nearby layers: their decoder directions stay near-identical or their activation patterns persist. They can be traced as paths across layers, along which a feature persists, merges with others or narrows to a more specific meaning.

examples.headline: Three bishop-movement features in different chess-model layers have highly similar decoders, which authors call cross-layer superposition.
On deeper layers, a layer-24 SAE keeps many of the same features active (adjacent-layer carry-over 0.72-0.82).
Per-layer Pythia SAE features best match the Group-SAE trained on the layer group containing their layer.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Feature granularity depends on sparsity setting, not only width
related_findings.summary: At equal reconstruction error, feature granularity depends on the sparsity setting (L0, the number of active features, or an L1 penalty) as well as on dictionary width. Choosing the SAE by minimum description length (MDL) can select an intermediate granularity.

examples.headline: Raising an InceptionV1 SAE's L1 penalty shifts activation from a double-curve feature to single-curve features.
The author states that sparser CLIP-embedding SAEs represent each concept with fewer, more generic features.
On MNIST at equal error, width and L0 set feature type; description-length minimization picks stroke-like features.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Opposite concepts may split into two non-negative SAE latents
related_findings.summary: SAEs with non-negative activations may split opposite (antipodal) concepts into two latents; signed latents can merge them in toy models with little superposition. In real SAEs, however, the two sides of a signed latent or a latent pair rarely form a clear, nameable opposition.

examples.headline: One signed AbsTopK SAE feature is positive for 'man', negative for 'woman', in otherwise identical inputs.
Signed latents merge antipodal pairs in low-superposition toys, but in audited real latents coherent oppositions are no more common than in random pairings.

reading_list.source_id: TITLE:Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
reading_list.why: The original account of feature splitting: one-layer transformer SAEs from 512 to 131,072 features, with qualitative splitting examples.
The original absorption study, with Gemma Scope and Llama 3.2 1B examples, toy models and the only causal ablation test of absorption.
Meta-SAEs and stitching latents across SAE sizes show larger SAEs add new and composite latents; no size gives canonical units.

known_gaps.summary: The evidence for feature splitting leans on a few overlapping groups, small or unstated model sizes and within-dictionary measures, and other explanations of what larger SAEs add have not been weighed against splitting.
items: Much of the real-model evidence for splitting and absorption comes from a few groups that overlap with the original authors, and some results appear twice, as a paper and as a blog post. Independent replication is thinner than the number of studies suggests.

Direct evidence that features split as open-release SAEs grow rests mainly on one hand-picked Llama-3.1-8B feature at one layer. Gemma Scope width series appear in other studies, but mostly for absorption or sensitivity rather than splitting itself.
Parent-child families have been measured inside a single dictionary. No study tests quantitatively whether features that split across dictionary sizes form such families.

Matryoshka-type and other objectives lower measured absorption in several studies, but independent evidence that they lower splitting in real models is weak. One independent study finds no change in split counts on Qwen3-8B, overlapping error intervals on Gemma-2-2B and single runs elsewhere, and its baseline for one setting is reported with two different values.

Absorption rates vary widely by model and setting, for example 0.0074 on Qwen3-8B vs 0.1908 on Gemma-2-2B in one study, and two studies on the same Gemma-2-2B layer and width, at different L0, report BatchTopK values of 0.49 and 0.19 that have not been reconciled. Only the original study tests absorption causally, by ablation.

Larger dictionaries may add dead, rare or insensitive latents, or tile continuous manifolds, rather than split coarse features into finer ones. These alternative readings have not been weighed against splitting.

No splitting or absorption test covers models above 10B parameters; larger models appear only in side results, such as steering on Llama-3.3-70b and script sharing on Gemma-3 up to 27B. Only one study varies width on an instruction-tuned model, many studies do not state model size, and the decomposition of large-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents is tested only on GPT-2 Small.
